figures: 1. Figure 1: Overview of Anisotropic Spectral Error Dressing (ASED). Given a deterministic GraphCast forecast, ASED: (1) computes spherical harmonic coefficients of historical residuals, (2) estimates degree spectrum C_l and within-degree anisotropy weights w_µ across 3 µ-bins and 4 degree bands, (3) generates M = 50 ensemble members by sampling Gaussian perturbations with the calibrated anisotropic spectral structure.

2. Figure 2: Scale-dependent anisotropy in GraphCast Z500 forecast errors. Each bar group shows the relative power in 3 µ-bins (zonal: µ < 0.33, intermediate: 0.33 ≤ µ < 0.67, meridional: µ ≥ 0.67) for 4 degree bands. Synoptic scales (l = 24–59) show the strongest anisotropy with zonal/meridional ratio of 5.99. Dashed line indicates isotropic reference (33.3 %).

3. Figure 3: CRPS improvement of ASED over SED by latitude band. ASED improves over SED across all latitude bands (82.4% of gridpoints), with the largest gains in the tropics (∆CRPS = 7.05) and consistent positive gains in extra-tropics (NH: 0.94, SH: 1.53). Green dashed line shows global mean improvement (3.17).
